messages:
Olivia: FYI ran the fused/paged attention perf sweep on the staging rtx-cluster and hit reproducible numeric blowups when fp8 is enabled for long sequences (>8k). logs attached in the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 :grimacing:

Samir: ugh. can you paste the failure output? is it NaNs from softmax or Inf?

Olivia: NaNs inside softmax for a handful of tokens, then attention outputs go insane. stack shows flashattn_fp8_kernel -> softmax_exp -> div by 0 pattern. sample log: ```EPOCH 0: step 12: attn_out nan at token=8123 QK_sum inf```

Keegan: interesting. we've seen softmax instability when the max is huge and we underflow/overflow in exp with low-precision. fp8 scaling behavior maybe too aggressive for paged-attn when kv pages concat causes large norms.

Maya: did the kernel selector fallback to a stable softmax variant? iirc we have a hysteresis rule to switch to bf16-softmax for sequences > 4k.

Olivia: selector did NOT switch. autotuner reported flash_gemm_fp8 as faster so it picked it. autotune outputs: ```chosen_kernel=flash_fp8_v2 latency=18.2ms score=0.92```

Samir: that means the kernel-selection heuristic is too throughput-biased and not accounting for numeric headroom. we should fold a numeric-safety score into the selector. quick fix: enforce softmax-precision safety copro for sequences > 6k or when max(abs(logits))>X.

Keegan: +1. Also KV cache paging may be changing magnitude distributions: when pages are concatenated we hit pathological Q/K scales. Could add per-page rescale before softmax or clamp logits with a small adaptive bias: logits = logits - max(logits) then clamp to >= -100.

Maya: for immediate mitigation, can we add a runtime fallback: if any exp produces inf/nan, re-run that batch with bf16-softmax and slower kernel. bench-bot can detect this and trigger a runtime switch.

bench-bot: auto-check: microbench on node gpu-07 for seq=8192, batch=2: flash_fp8_v2: 17.9ms (nan rate 0.002), bf16-fused: 34.1ms (nan rate 0.0).

Olivia: ok provable tradeoff. but we also have a perf regression in the paged-attn hot path after the fp8 kernel landed — ~7% latency regression for seq < 2k on small batches. suspect branching in kernel selector added overhead.

Samir: can you bisect the PR range? which commit introduced the selector change?

Olivia: suspect range is 2024-11-PR#842 (kernel-autotune-refactor). will start bisect tomorrow. quick profiling shows extra 500us in selection logic per request when batch sizes are tiny.

Keegan: we should memoize kernel decisions keyed by (model-id, seq_len_bucket, dtype_profile, kv_layout_hash). that would shave repeated decision costs for steady-state traffic. also add cache invalidation after model rollout.

Maya: on the numeric side, propose two changes: (1) add an epsilon floor inside exp path for fp8 path i.e. exp(clamped_logits) with clamp to [-80, 80] and (2) track running max of logits in the KV cache pages and emit a per-page normalization when attaching pages. both are low-risk.

Olivia: implemented local patch for clamp to [-80, 80] + runtime fallback to bf16 on nan — retested, NaNs gone on 8192 seq, latency penalty ~+1.2ms versus previous fp8 success runs. seems acceptable for safety. PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1786

Samir: nice. let's also add an offline eval harness that runs synthetic kernels across seq distribution observed in the wild and flags any numeric instability. we can incorporate that into the model-boarding checklist.

Keegan: agree. one more thought: batching heuristics can exacerbate this — heavy fusion (coalescing many short requests into one large effective seq) will amplify logits. we should cap auto-batching by effective-token-length or force per-request normalization prior to concatenate.

Maya: noted. i'll add a heuristic: if combined_seq > page_size and max_logit_range across requests > threshold, disable aggressive coalesce.

Olivia: ok i pushed the emergency clamp+fallback PR and added bench runs. will follow up with bisect results and a proposal for selector numeric-safety score. thanks all :rocket:

Keegan: great. follow-up todo: (1) memoize selector decisions (2) add softmax clamp + per-page norm (3) offline instability harness (4) update rollout docs. I'll create tickets.

bench-bot: ticket created: INF-2218 (kernel selector memoization), INF-2219 (softmax clamp+page-norm), INF-2220 (instability harness), INF-2221 (batching coalesce cap).

Samir: can someone add a short note to release notes warning about the fp8 behavior and the temporary rollback option? ops might want the flag.

Olivia: will add release note blurb and ops runbook entry. For now marking the incident as mitigated by runtime fallback. :white_check_mark:
